# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Economic Policy
The manifesto proposes cutting employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027 and abolishing self-employed National Insurance entirely. The party commits to not raising income tax, VAT, or corporation tax. A "Triple Lock Plus" would ensure state pensions and pensioner tax allowances rise annually by the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%.

## Taxation and Families
Child Benefit thresholds would shift to household-based assessment, with withdrawal beginning at £120,000 combined income. Working parents would receive 30 hours of free childcare weekly from nine months until school age.

## Immigration
A legal cap on migration would be introduced with annual parliamentary votes. The Rwanda removal scheme would continue for illegal migrants. Visa fees would increase, and health checks would be required for incoming migrants.

## Defence and Security
Defence spending would reach 2.5% of GDP by 2030, with £10 billion invested in munitions production. Support for Ukraine would continue at current levels.

## Housing
The party targets 1.6 million new homes, with permanent Stamp Duty abolition for first-time buyers on properties up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme.

## Healthcare
NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with plans for 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 more doctors. Mental health support in schools would expand to 100% coverage by 2030.

## Energy
Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing rounds would continue. Small Modular Reactor fleets would be approved, and offshore wind capacity would triple. Green levies on household bills would be kept lower than 2023 levels.

## Young People
Mandatory National Service would be introduced for 18-year-olds, offering either military placement or community volunteering. 100,000 additional apprenticeships would be funded by closing underperforming university courses.
